intro:
You settle the security configuration of a service from policies, standards, runbooks and chat. They often disagree.

Initial specification:
- [e001] Precedence rule: when sources disagree, the order of authority is security-policy > standard > runbook > wiki > chat. Inside one source, the higher version wins.
- [e002] According to standard STD-1 version 1, the default currency is `CHF`.
- [e003] According to standard STD-1 version 1, the data residency region is `us-zone`.
- [e004] According to standard STD-1 version 1, the session timeout in minutes is `60`.
- [e005] According to standard STD-1 version 1, the export file format is `csv`.
- [e006] According to standard STD-1 version 1, the strict validation mode is `OFF`.
- [e007] The standard document STD-1 (version 1) states that the data retention in days is `30`.
- [e008] The standard document STD-1 (version 1) states that the minimum TLS version is `tls-1.1`.
- [e009] The standard document STD-1 (version 1) states that the password hash algorithm is `argon2id`.
- [e010] According to runbook RB-105 version 1, the API rate limit per minute is `300`.

Sources, from highest to lowest authority: security-policy, standard, runbook, wiki, chat. When two sources disagree, the higher one decides.
Inside one source, a higher version number overrides a lower one. A withdrawn document no longer counts at all.
Every event has a label of the form [eNNN] with a three-digit number. A higher number is later in time. A later event can change or cancel an earlier one.
Some material quotes old pages or copies for history. A quote of that kind is not a new statement.
